- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.70) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–3% of recent mean or median.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often over-optimistically forecasts continuation; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment alternates between positive/negative with no clear trend, model exhibits mean-reversion bias; use 15-day rolling mean as anchor for correction.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% for 3+ consecutive days, model is under-reacting to sentiment; increase forecast by 2–5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.50) and forecast is still rising, model is ignoring sentiment; reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until sentiment reverses or price stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility; add 1–2% buffer to forecast if sentiment is volatile or recent price range >±5%.
- If sentiment is positive but price is flat or declining, model is overconfident; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid “sentiment trap”.
- When sentiment is neutral (±0.30) and price is trending, model often misses momentum; use 7-day momentum as signal to adjust forecast direction.
